title: The four consumed reads and the two handed-over operations of the pack carry no dependency row, and two of the operations have no published name
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-05, DP-07, DP-08, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-19 and section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5004-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5004-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract, Integration and External dependencies None) and of RWB-S4-E5004-CON (all three None); TSD S4 v2 T5.2 (P3 for the case, P5 for documents) and T-A.1; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 API-P5-002 and API-P5-008; TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 API-P3-002; FSD S4 v3 A2.4.2 (integration points: Workbench, the Workbench document hub, CCMS); legacy RWB-E5-004 Depends on FEAT-DCM-02
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of both stories; the metadata table and the two fragments
description: The two stories consume four things and hand over two, and no metadata row carries any of them. (1) The document index of rwb-document on API-P5-002 and the checklist on API-P5-008, both built in Epic 1 under FEAT-DCM-02, the legacy prerequisite of the key. (2) The case facts of rwb-case on API-P3-002. (3) The case state announcement that carries NOTICE_BLOCKED and PACK_VERIFIED, because the states of R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-16 are the case of record's and not values of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS. (4) The task raise for the litigation officer, because the task table is P3's. (5) The reference read of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, because DP-07 is not in the pattern set while TSD S4 T3.2 makes both lists required. (6) The declared Litigation right of each operation, because DP-08 is not in the pattern set. Items 3 and 4 also have no published operation name in any source: Architecture v5 and TSD P3 describe the case move and the task in prose only, so both carry the placeholder in both stories. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the pack needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-08 adds H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 only; the dependency rows of both stories name no contract, integration or external dependency; TSD S4 v2 T5.2 names P3, P5, P6 and P7 as the cross-module interfaces and T-A.1 lists no operation of rwb-case; TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 lists API-P3-002 GET /cases/{caseId} and the task operations but no case-move or state-announcement operation; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P5-002 and API-P5-008; the legacy metadata names FEAT-DCM-02 and no other dependency
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document, P3 rwb-case and P4 rwb-access
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P5 rwb-document, P3 rwb-case and P4 rwb-access architects and the platform team
proposed: Carry the consumed reads as non-blocking rows in the Dependency Map: API-P5-002, API-P5-008 and API-P3-002 on their published contracts built against their fakes, the reference-data read as a C dependency of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the declared right as the edge and guard rule of DP-08; name the case-state announcement and the task raise in the P3 case contract when it is next versioned, and leave the metadata rows of the plan as they are.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-004, so both stories trace to the feature only
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-004 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-04, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-DCM-02, Decision); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-004 with reqs = []; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-04; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010, none naming the pack)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-004 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-04 and the prerequisite FEAT-DCM-02 and no requirement row, the plan's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the FSD S4 requirements table lists ten requirements of the module whose texts cover notices, the pack check, the panel, court tracking, settlement, enforcement, deferral, prescription and proceeds but not the assembly of the pack. The Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-04 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce, and the requirement column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds the identifiers. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report that cannot roll the story up to a requirement.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-004 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index of the run records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 with no pack-assembly requirement; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-04 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind System, primary role RW-LITOFF, systems Workbench, the Workbench document hub and CCMS, depends on FEAT-DCM-02 and no requirement
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Add one requirement row to the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and to the S4 module trace, covering the pack as a composition of the document index and the case facts with the withdrawn-template hold, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it exists.

title: The pack has no table in the Ownership Map and no object in TSD S4 T3.1, so where an assembled pack is held is not stated by any source
source: Ownership Map v1 rows owned by S4 (tables: hearing, legal_action); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action and hearing only) and T3.3 (three relationships, none of them a pack); FSD S4 v3 A2.4.2 (the pack is built from the document index and the case facts) and A2.4.3.1; legacy RWB-E5-004 Data block (recovery_case, task, legal_action, notice, document, decision_log_entry)
section: Sections 2, 8, 11, 12.7 and 13 of both stories; the ops_provided and workflows keys of both fragments
description: The pack is the central object of the legacy key and it has no home in the target: the Ownership Map gives this service two tables, legal_action and hearing, and TSD S4 T3.1 declares the same two objects, so no pack, pack_item or pack_checklist table exists and no column of legal_action holds the composition. The legacy Data block also names no pack entity: it names the case, the task, the legal action, the notice, the document and the decision log entry. Both stories therefore treat the pack as derived on every read from API-P5-002 and API-P5-008 and from API-P3-002, declare the pack sub-shape as read-only elements of the legal-action answer, and record no pack row. Two consequences follow and are stated rather than decided: an assembly leaves no persisted pack, so what the officer verified is reconstructed from the decision record, the index and the case state; and a future requirement to freeze a verified pack as at the verification time has no shape to write it to.
evidence: Ownership Map v1: S4 owns hearing and legal_action, two tables; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 gives legal_action (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029) and T3.3 gives legal_action to recovery_case, legal_action to partner and hearing to legal_action; the legacy Data block lists six entities and none is a pack; FSD S4 A2.4.2 names the document hub and CCMS as the integration points and no pack store
area: Data model and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document
owner_role: Solution architect and data steward, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P5 rwb-document data owner
proposed: Keep the pack derived and say so in the Service Contract Catalog and the S4 data model; if a verified pack must be frozen, add a pack snapshot object to the Ownership Map and a column or table with its own DB story, and change the two stories and their fragments at that point.

title: NOTICE_BLOCKED, PACK_ASSEMBLY, PACK_VERIFIED and PACK_DEFECT_HOLD are moved by the litigation rules but are not values of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, and no source says which object holds them
source: TSD S4 v2 T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-STATUS: OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN) and T4 (the rule table with PACK_ASSEMBLY, PACK_VERIFIED, NOTICE_BLOCKED and PACK_DEFECT_HOLD as from and to states); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-04, R-LIT-15, R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17 and R-LIT-21; Architecture v5 slide 10 (rwb_case holds case, stage and tasks) and slide 3 notes (the stage clock); the legacy acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 (the case moves to NOTICE_BLOCKED and to PACK_VERIFIED)
section: Sections 2, 8, 9 and 12.2 of both stories; BR3 and BR4 of each; AC5 of the contract story
description: The rules of this key move a case between four states that appear nowhere in LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, the only status list this service has. Two readings are possible: the four states are stages or states of the case of record, which is what the legacy acceptance criteria say in words (the case moves to NOTICE_BLOCKED), or they are a second status ladder of the legal action, which the list forbids. Neither TSD S4 T4 nor the Business Rules extract names the object that holds them, and no source gives the operation or the event by which rwb-case accepts the move. Both stories therefore read the four as states of the case of record, announce them to rwb-case as state facts with the rule ID and its version, declare no seventh status value, and carry the operation name and the answer field list as the placeholder.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.2 LOV-LEGAL-STATUS has six members and none of the four states; TSD S4 v2 T4 gives the five rules with the four states as from and to; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-LIT-04 to NOTICE_BLOCKED, R-LIT-15 to PACK_ASSEMBLY, R-LIT-16 to PACK_VERIFIED, R-LIT-17 to PACK_DEFECT_HOLD and R-LIT-21 back to PACK_ASSEMBLY with owners Litigation officer and service levels of 1, 3, 2, 5 and 1 working days; Architecture v5 slide 10 puts the case, the stage and the tasks in rwb_case; TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 lists no state-announcement operation
area: State model and case contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case analyst and the Business Rules owner
proposed: Confirm that the four states are case states or stage codes of rwb-case, name them in the case state list of the P3 contract, and publish the state-announcement operation and its answer shape there; if instead any of them becomes a legal_action status, extend LOV-LEGAL-STATUS with its own version and change the two stories and the contract story in one major version.

title: The pack has no operation of its own in any source, and the legacy endpoint block names the notice approval, which belongs to the notice stories of the service
source: Legacy RWB-E5-004 Endpoints block (POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve, Litigation A; POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, Litigation C); TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005, none of them a pack operation); Ownership Map v1 REST operations provided by S4 (5, including POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve); FSD S4 v3 A2.1 to A2.3 (the notice features)
section: Sections 2, 12.1 and 19 of both stories; the ops_provided key of both fragments; AC1 of the contract story
description: The legacy story of the pack names two endpoints: the approval of a generated notice with right A and the creation of a legal action with right C. Neither is a pack operation, and the TSD inventory has no pack path at all. The notice approval is the operation of the demand-notice features FEAT-LIT-01 to FEAT-LIT-03, whose stories are separate from this key, so declaring it here would publish an operation another story builds; omitting it leaves the legacy endpoint row of this key with no story of its own. The two stories therefore publish the three legal-action operations that exist in the TSD and name the notice approval and the hearing operations as other stories', and the question whether the pack should be a resource with its own operation is left open rather than answered by a new path.
evidence: The legacy Endpoints block of RWB-E5-004 has two rows and neither path names a pack; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 has five operations and no pack path; the Ownership Map gives S4 five operations of which API-S4-001 is the notice approval; FSD S4 v3 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.3 are the notice features whose stories own it; FSD S4 v3 A2.4 gives no endpoint for FEAT-LIT-04
area: API surface and story boundary, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the API owner of the Service Contract Catalog
proposed: Record in the Service Contract Catalog that the pack is a read view of the legal action and has no operation of its own, and that API-S4-001 is owned by the notice stories of this service; if the pack must later be addressed as a resource, add the operation to the TSD inventory first and then to a contract story, so that no two stories publish one path.

title: No source names the trigger of the pack assembly, and the service owns no event although the catalogue lists three on its topic
source: Legacy RWB-E5-004 AC1 ('When its trigger arrives'); FSD S4 v3 A2.4.2 (step 1: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer; integration points Workbench, the Workbench document hub, CCMS); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-15 (NOTICE_PERIOD_EXPIRED opens PACK_ASSEMBLY); Ownership Map v1 events owned by S4 (0); Architecture v5 event catalogue rows for LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult on rwb.litigation.events.v1; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set of this key (DP03, DP13, DP19)
section: Sections 2, 4, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5 and 13 of both stories; the events_published and workflows keys of both fragments
description: AC1 fires on 'its trigger' and no source says what the trigger is: FSD S4 A2.4.2 describes the generic step pattern of the module (a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer) without naming one for the pack, R-LIT-15 opens PACK_ASSEMBLY on the expiry of the notice period and belongs to the notice-period story, and no job or Schedule is assigned to this service. At the same time the Ownership Map gives the service no event while the catalogue lists three on its topic, so a reader may expect the assembly to raise one. Both stories therefore build the assembly as a step of LitigationWorkflow started from the case state and the template status, declare no event and no Schedule, and carry the assembly activity name and the trigger as the placeholder.
evidence: Legacy AC1 line 'When its trigger arrives'; FSD S4 A2.4.2 step 1 and the generic integration points; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-15 is the only rule that opens PACK_ASSEMBLY and its event is the notice period expiry; Ownership Map v1 events owned by S4: 0 and jobs owned by S4: 0; the catalogue lists LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult on rwb.litigation.events.v1; DP-09 is not in the pattern set of either story
area: Workflow, scheduling and event contract, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the Temporal workflow owner and the event platform owner
proposed: Name the trigger in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog: either the case-state fact of R-LIT-15 or an explicit start signal on the litigation workflow, with the assembly activity and its queue named; decide once whether any of the three catalogue events is raised by a pack assembly, and if none is, record the empty producer in the catalogue row so that the gap does not reopen.

title: The index set of legal_action, the business text of the 400 and 409 answers, and the source of the defect-list items are not stated in any source read for this key
source: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 and T3.0 (columns and standard columns, no index set); TSD S4 v2 T-A.2 (error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 with no 400 row and no message text); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-16 (condition 'every defect list item present') and R-LIT-17 (one or more defect list items missing); FSD S4 v3 A2.4.3.1 (VR-S4-004-1 stale data product) and A2.5 (the defect list check, FEAT-LIT-05); legacy RWB-E5-004 Validation and messages block
section: Sections 8, 12.8, 13 and 14 of both stories; AC3 and AC4 of the contract story; section 11 of both stories
description: Three values the build needs are absent from every source read for this key. (1) The index set of legal_action beyond its primary key: the TSD gives the columns and the standard columns and no index, while the workspace reads by case and the pack view reads by legal action, so at least two lookups have no declared index. (2) The business text and the allocated message ID of the 400 that a malformed body produces and of the 409 that a refused state fact produces: the TSD gives the status list and no text, and no row of the legacy message set matches either condition. (3) The defect-list items that R-LIT-16's condition names: the list belongs to FEAT-LIT-05 and to RWB-S4-E5005-APP, and no source read here defines its members. Both stories write the placeholder for all three rather than invent a value, declare only the primary key in the template, and evaluate the completeness check against the published checklist of API-P5-008.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 and T3.0 list columns only; TSD S4 v2 T-A.2 gives six error statuses per operation and no 400 row and no message text; the legacy Validation and messages block gives MSG-S4-001, MSG-S4-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 and no 400 or 409 text; FSD S4 A2.5 (FEAT-LIT-05) owns the defect list and gives no members; FSD S4 A2.4.3.1 gives VR-S4-004-1 for stale data only
area: Physical schema and API detail, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect and DB owner, S4 rwb-litigation, with the message catalogue owner and the RWB-S4-E5005-APP analyst
proposed: Publish the index set with the physical schema file of rwb_litigation, add the two missing message IDs and their texts to the message catalogue, and name the defect-list items in the RWB-S4-E5005-APP story and its reference data; then replace the placeholders in the two stories, the contract template and the fragments.
